hyp_1.title: Telemetry tracking loss
hyp_1.explanation: Client-side event tracking dropped events so reported metrics fell.

history.reason: tracking_gap_check result contradicts the hypothesis (capture rates are consistent across segments (min p=1))

hyp_2.title: Code regression in a release
hyp_2.explanation: A recent release introduced a bug that broke part of checkout.

history.reason: Under active analysis; evidence ev_2_d8fd recorded (supports).

hyp_3.title: Traffic mix shift
hyp_3.explanation: The mix of arriving users shifted toward lower-converting segments.

history.reason: mix_shift_decomposition result contradicts the hypothesis (mix effect -0.000143 explains little of -0.0295)

hyp_4.title: Third-party outage
hyp_4.explanation: An external payment dependency failed for a short period.

history.reason: Under active analysis; evidence ev_4_3ef6 recorded (supports).
spike_check result contradicts the hypothesis (no single abnormal day (0 day(s) with raw p<0.001))

hyp_5.title: Seasonality or calendar effect
hyp_5.explanation: The comparison window covers weekends or holidays that are normally quieter.

history.reason: seasonal_baseline result contradicts the hypothesis (deviation from same-weekday baseline remains (p=2.55e-08) or no weekday pattern (p=0.431))

hyp_6.title: Natural variation
hyp_6.explanation: The change is within normal day-to-day variation of the metric.

history.reason: change_point result contradicts the hypothesis (a change point exists (p=0.002))

hyp_7.title: Pricing or policy change
hyp_7.explanation: A price or policy change reduced conversion.

hyp_8.title: Gradual cohort decay
hyp_8.explanation: Retention is eroding gradually across cohorts.

history.reason: Under active analysis; evidence ev_7_9586 recorded (supports).
change_point result supports the hypothesis (gradual decline, no single step) [rule: 2+ supporting items from 2+ analyses, significant after correction]

supported_causes.statement: The evidence is consistent with Code regression in a release (code_regression); the available tools cannot confirm the underlying cause, accounting for about 211% of the observed change (estimate -0.4397 +/- 0.109 SE, method difference_in_differences:exposed_share_weighted).

The evidence is consistent with Gradual cohort decay (gradual_or_cohort_effect); the available tools cannot confirm the underlying cause; its contribution to the observed change could not be quantified.
